Follow it with coverage_status, whose `job` carries its state, each tool's start and outcome, and once completed the run's outcomes: ran, tests_failed (the suite failed but wrote a report, which is ingested), failed (a masked stderr excerpt; the whole output in a log under .logos/coverage/), timed_out, cancelled, or not_applicable / disabled / not_installed. A run builds the project and runs its tests, so it executes the project's own code: it runs only under the project's coverage execution consent (FR-CV-13), which only the user can record, with `logos coverage run --consent` in a terminal; without it, it starts no job and returns that instruction. description:
The branch delta (FR-GV-24): every offender (all nine dimensions, uncapped) and every check violation, classified new, worsened, improved, resolved or unchanged PER SYMBOL against the merge-base of HEAD and `base` (default: the repository's default branch). Changed entries are listed; unchanged ones are only counted (offender_counts, violation_counts). Each entry carries its value before and after, its threshold, and a trust label: resolved, stale (the file changed since the last sync — run sync), or the tag of a language the graph binds within files only. Also lists near-clone groups the branch introduced; `attribution` breaks the signal's change into per-dimension contributions in log space (points summing to exact_change, with the integer rounding and the residual stated), each naming its top driving symbols or clone groups, capped, with driver_count; and under sections.security the security findings the branch introduced, touched or resolved (FR-SC-18): each with its method (fingerprint against the report recorded at the merge-base, else hunk), freshness, severity, OWASP categories and reachability confidence; a finding removed on a file edited since the last scan reads stale, never resolved; suppressed findings are listed apart; messages stay redacted; never scanned reads measured:false. The before-state is the snapshot recorded at the merge-base, else a shadow index of that tree cached by commit (the first call may take as long as an index); no other commit is ever compared. Advisory: never moves check or gate. measured:false with not_measured_because means nothing was classified. Byte-stable; the CLI twin is `logos review --base `. With `branches` (FR-GV-28) it instead sums each branch's delta against `base` (tip minus merge-base, every side a committed tree) and projects it onto the shared limits — every projectable [constraints] budget, per module, function, file or project-wide count, and a numeric [review] drift_budget, whose drift is judged from this checkout's comparable gate baseline (else the base commit's signal; `drift.reference` and a note say which), so the answer depends on that baseline: `exceeded` (and `drift`) list each limit the combined merge would exceed, with every branch's share and whether it alone would; `subjects` is the denominator; a branch that cannot be measured is named in `branches` with why and left out of the sum; `not_projected` names declared limits it does not judge. Report only; the CLI twin is `logos review --base --branches `. With `headroom: true` (FR-GV-29) it instead lists, before any branch exists, the room left under every budget `branches` projects, on the same base and from the same cached measurement: each subject's current value, allowance and headroom (negative when the base is already past it) and its kind (limit, or ratchet against its blessed value read at the base commit), under `rules` with each rule's `evaluated` denominator and `listed` count — the 10 tightest per rule, or only the ones `subjects` (project-relative file paths and symbol names; each resolves to its module, file and functions) and `near` (at most that much room) select; entries that resolve to nothing are under `unresolved` with why; `drift` gives the margin under a numeric drift_budget; `not_projected` names the budgets it does not list. The working tree is never measured; `base_commit` names the tree. Report only: measured:false (base unresolved) means nothing was listed; the CLI twin is `logos review --headroom [--base ] [--subjects

…] [--near N]`.

description: Deep graph consistency check (FR-GV-19, NFR-RA-06): reindexes the project into a throwaway shadow store via the always-purge index path, then diffs node/edge/file counts and symbol sets against the live graph. Reports `ok:false` with live-vs-reindex deltas and a capped sample of leaked (live-only) / orphaned (reindex-only) symbols, and embeds the fast structural + admission check (FR-GV-20). Catches Channel-B orphans (files the live store retains but a fresh index drops) that doctor cannot. On-demand only — a full reindex is seconds-to-minutes; the live store is read-only and the shadow store is torn down on completion. Under a workspace it acts on the default member only: it takes no `repo`.
name: verify
